answers.explanation: Programs see a uniform interface; drivers deal with the quirks.
A buffer holds data in transit, like a video player loading ahead.
A cache holds a copy of data that also lives somewhere slower.
Print jobs are queued on disk while the printer works through them.
Only the driver knows its device; the rest of the kernel uses the general interface.
Every driver provides the same standard functions.
The jobs wait in the spool on disk, and the printer takes them one at a time.
